massing.relative_position: east side facing the apron/ramp; the tallest element of the complex

massing.role: single-story ground-boarding gate concourse (no jet bridges as built)
massing.relative_position: extends north/south along the apron from the two-story lounge
massing.notes: Ribbon of holdroom windows, each bay sheltered by a repeating sloped green metal gate canopy; ground-level boarding via covered walkways to aircraft.

massing.role: air traffic control tower (separate structure, not part of terminal)
massing.relative_position: near the terminal, set back from the curb
massing.notes: Slender dark shaft with glazed cab; a strong vertical landmark next to the low terminal. Model as a distinct object.

heights.method: Scaled against the airside photo: fuel/box truck box height ~3.3 m and United CRJ fuselage/tail for the apron; single-story gate-concourse eave read ~5 m and the two-story glazed departure-lounge roof ~10-11 m (~2x the concourse). Landside gable ridges lower, ~7-9 m; landside eaves ~3.5-4.5 m. Standard 2.1 m doors used as secondary scale. Estimates +/-20%.

landside_vs_airside: Landside (west/curb) reads as a low, rustic lodge: several stepped green metal gables, tan walls, dark stone piers, exposed glulam, and a projecting entry canopy over the drop-off. Airside (east/apron) is taller and more modern: a two-story fully glazed departure lounge under a deep cantilevered green roof on tapered concrete piers, with a single-story gate concourse of repeating sloped canopies. The green standing-seam roof and material palette unify both faces.

landside_entry_canopy.form: projecting gable/curved green metal canopy over the curbside drop-off

airside_gate_canopies.form: repeating sloped (mono-pitch) green metal canopies, one per holdroom/gate bay
airside_gate_canopies.support: steel/concrete posts and cantilevers off the concourse

airside_main_overhang.form: deep cantilevered roof eave over the two-story glazed lounge

design_narrative.landside_gabled_building_architect: Barber Barrett Turner Architects (per Kirby Nagelhout Construction portfolio); general contractor Kirby Nagelhout Construction Company
design_narrative.landside_building_material_intent: Stated palette: 'an exposed glu-lam structure, natural wood finishes, and stone masonry throughout' (Kirby Nagelhout portfolio).
design_narrative.2009_expansion_architect: HNTB (per Wikipedia / Roberts Field); ~600% area increase, bi-level structure with a two-story windowed departure lounge and covered walkways to aircraft; opened October 2009.
design_narrative.current_terminal_size: ~132,000 sq ft, described as showcasing Central Oregon design elements.
design_narrative.future_expansion_not_built: A separate $180-200M, 80,000+ sq ft concourse expansion (Hennebery Eddy Architects + RS&H; builder Skanska) broke ground ~2025 for ~2028 completion, adding a second-level concourse with seven jet bridges, mass-timber ceilings and curtain-wall with Cascade-silhouette solar shade fins. This is NOT reflected in the reference photos and should NOT be modeled as existing.

confidence.per_section_notes: Massing/roof forms: HIGH (clear in airside ramp photo, oblique aerial, entry close-up, orthophoto). Colors: MEDIUM - green roof/fascia and dark tinted glass sampled directly (roof ~#6b786e sunlit, airside glass ~#2c3845); landside glass reads greener/teal (~#6f8f8e); tan wall and glulam amber are observational, not cleanly sampled (small/JPEG images, varied lighting). Heights: MEDIUM-LOW, scaled from vehicles/aircraft/doors, +/-20%. Two build eras present (pre-2009 landside gabled building + 2009 HNTB airside expansion); reconcile the two faces when modeling.
